newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Main events in Yeltsin's political career.
newsitem.headline: Main events in Yeltsin's political career.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin returned to the Kremlin on Monday after seven weeks convalescing from open heart surgery. Here is an outline of his political career.
1985 - New Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev brings Yeltsin, a Communist Party boss in the Urals city of Sverdlovsk, to Moscow to oversee construction. He then becomes Moscow city party boss.
February 1986 - Yeltsin is made a candidate member of the politburo, the inner cabinet of the Soviet Union's ruling party.
October 1987 - Yeltsin is sacked from the politburo in disgrace after complaining at the slow pace of reform. He is taken to hospital after suffering a breakdown.
March 1989 - Yeltsin is elected to the Soviet Congress of People's Deputies, Gorbachev's new-style parliament.
March 1990 - He is elected from Sverdlovsk to the Russian Federation's Congress of People's Deputies.
May 1990 - The Russian Congress elects Yeltsin as chairman.
June 1990 - Yeltsin quits the Communist Party.
June 1991 - Yeltsin becomes Russia's first directly elected president, defeating communist and nationalist candidates.
August 1991 - Yeltsin plays a key role in putting down a hardline coup against Gorbachev and he soon eclipses his rival.
October 1991 - Yeltsin announces plans for radical reforms with a team headed by little-known economist Yegor Gaidar.
December 1991 - Yeltsin and the leaders of Belarus and Ukraine sign agreement ending Soviet Union. Gorbachev resigns.
June 1992 - Yeltsin appoints Gaidar acting prime minister.
December 1992 - Yeltsin, facing opposition from a conservative parliament to Gaidar's reforms, drops Gaidar and replaces him with former gas industry boss Viktor Chernomyrdin.
March 1993 - Yeltsin survives an impeachment bid by the Russian parliament.
April 1993 - He wins a national referendum on confidence in his rule.
September 1993 - Yeltsin dissolves parliament, accusing it of blocking constitutional reforms and elections. Rebel deputies barricade themselves inside the White House parliament building.
October 1993 - Supporters of parliament stage an armed attack on the Moscow TV station. The following day Yeltsin uses tanks to storm the White House and put down the rebellion.
December 1993 - Voters approve a constitution giving Yeltsin increased powers. They select a new parliament, the State Duma.
February 1994 - The Duma amnesties Ruslan Khasbulatov and Alexander Rutskoi, who led rebel deputies in the October parliamentary crisis.
December 1994 - Yeltsin sends troops into separatist Chechnya. Tens of thousands are killed in 21 months of fighting.
July 1995 - Yeltsin is taken to hospital with heart problems. He stays there for two weeks and then moves to a sanatorium to continue his recovery.
October 1995 - Yeltsin has a second heart attack. He does not return to the Kremlin until December 29.
December 1995 - Communists win more than one-third of seats in elections to a new Duma.
January 1996 - Yeltsin ousts several liberals, including privatisation chief Anatoly Chubais.
February 1996 - Yeltsin says he will run for a second term in office and launches an active Western-style campaign.

June 1996 - Yeltsin takes first place in the first round of the election ahead of communist Gennady Zyuganov. He appoints third-placed candidate Alexander Lebed his security adviser. In late June he cancels campaign trips, aides say he is tired.
July 1996 - Yeltsin wins a second term in office, coming in 13 points ahead of Zyuganov.
August 1996 - Yeltsin takes his oath of office in a brief Kremlin ceremony. But he moves stiffly and looks unwell.
September 1996 - Yeltsin tells the nation he has agreed to have heart surgery to enable him to live a normal life. Doctors say it will take six weeks to prepare him for the operation.
October 1996 - Yeltsin sacks Lebed in a televised address. He accuses the general of harbouring presidential ambitions and splitting the Kremlin team.
November 1996 - Yeltsin undergoes a quintuple bypass operation. His convalescence takes place at hospitals and official residences outside Moscow.
December 1996 - Yeltsin, returning to work in the Kremlin, promises to be an "active and energetic president". REUTER
